$comment: Per-checker configuration for this repo. Each checker falls back to its own defaults when its key is absent, so deleting a block degrades to the built-in behaviour rather than to an empty scope. What lives here is what changes between repos: layout, thresholds, and the regexes that name one stack's idioms. What stays in code is the rule itself.
$profile: The shape this repo claims to hold, not the tools it uses: baseline = one axis measures · standard = two axes block, both meta-checks present · hardened = every declared axis blocks and every gate job is asserted. A profile is a claim someone else can fail you on, which is the only kind worth writing down.
$baselines: Level 2 means `baseline the old, block the new`, so an axis at 2 must name WHERE its debt is frozen and WHICH direction counts as improvement — otherwise the frozen number is a photograph nobody can compare against. `improves`: down = a per-key number may only decrease · shrink = a set may only lose members · tighten = a status may only move to the stricter value. The direction lives here rather than inside the baseline file because `--update-baseline` rewrites those files, and a rule that a re-freeze can silently drop is not a rule.

form.owns: file & function length; whitespace, import order, recommended rules

knowledge.owns: cm: couplings, prose discipline, module headers; whether a document asking to be adopted prices what adopting it costs; whether a doc injected into every session names the pipeline mode its status transitions belong to

relations.owns: which module may depend on which

alsoBaseline.$why: archmap lock writes this, and without a direction that command is an amnesty button: run it and today's violations stop blocking. `down` means the frozen TOTAL may not rise and no per-key count may rise, so freezing a new file in fails and letting a blob grow inside its own entry fails, while fixing one and re-freezing is free.

behaviour.owns: whether a test asserts behaviour or restates a declaration; whether every declared flow step is executed end-to-end; whether every tracked test file is collected by a runner at all

record.owns: whether the external record of what shipped keeps the heading its readers parse for, and whether an entry once published can be removed without saying so
record.$why: The other five axes each own a property of the CODE. On 2026-08-28 commit 3df9a8e9 removed 1,034 lines from CHANGELOG.md inside a docs-pointer commit whose message never named the file; twelve gates ran and every one passed, because the record was nobody's. No baseline: it starts at zero debt, and a removal is declared per-instance in .forge/changelog-amnesty.json rather than frozen in bulk — a public record is edited one line at a time or not at all.

archmap.$comment: Ceiling on edges `arch check` cannot resolve. Measured 2026-08-23: 171, all of them node_modules subpath exports (hono/http-exception and friends), which belong to no module and so cannot violate a contract. It was 997 until `.arch.json` declared a tsConfig — 841 of those were web-v2's `@/*` alias, and an unresolvable edge is DROPPED, so three locked contracts over that package were being checked against an empty graph. Audit rule R7 fails if it climbs back.

lint-budget.$comment: Registering a class is this list plus one `--update-baseline` run — no second script, no second baseline file. That is the whole claim ISS-833 made for a shared ratchet, and `packages/core` is the proof of it: its `warn`-severity rules produced 280 diagnostics that nothing counted, because biome exits 0 on a warning. A scope with no `drain` block is freeze-only.
lint-budget.$drain: Freezing does not reduce — the codemap baseline sat frozen for months at 3% drained. `drain` adds the rule that does: a file in the branch delta matching `include` and not `exclude`, whose baseline count is above zero, must come back STRICTLY lower. web-v2 declares none on purpose: 98 debt-carrying files with the formatter deliberately off is a separate decision from turning the linter on.
